rows.note: Use 入錢 as the everyday verb for putting money into a bank account or other account.

example.english: I need to deposit money into my account today.
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam1 jat6 jiu3 jap6 cin2 lok6 wu6 hau2

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose noun for money kept in a bank account.

example.english: My bank deposit still isn't enough to buy a flat.
example.traditional: 我啲銀行存款暫時仲未夠買樓。
example.jyutping: ngo5 di1 ngan4 hong4 cyun4 fun2 zaam6 si4 zung6 mei6 gau3 maai5 lau4

rows.note: Use this for money paid in advance to reserve or purchase something.

example.english: You have to pay a thirty-percent deposit first when buying a flat.
example.traditional: 買樓嗰陣要先俾三成訂金。
example.jyutping: maai5 lau4 go2 zan6 jiu3 sin1 bei2 saam1 sing4 deng6 gam1

rows.note: Use 放 as the all-purpose verb for placing something somewhere, including ordinary storage; use 收埋 when putting it away for safekeeping is emphasized.

example.english: You can deposit the book on the table for now.
example.traditional: 你可以將本書放喺張枱度先。
example.jyutping: nei5 ho2 ji5 zoeng1 bun2 syu1 fong3 hai2 zoeng1 toi2 dou6 sin1

rows.note: Use this when the money is refundable after a borrowed item or property is returned.

example.english: You need to pay a deposit to rent this camera, and you'll get it back when you return it.
example.traditional: 租呢部相機要俾按金，還機嗰陣會退返畀你。
example.jyutping: zou1 ni1 bou6 soeng2 gei1 jiu3 bei2 on3 gam1 waan4 gei1 go2 zan6 wui5 teoi3 faan1 bei2 nei5

rows.note: Use 收埋 when goods are being put away or kept somewhere safely, often out of sight.

example.english: We need to deposit the cash somewhere safe so no one sees it.
example.traditional: 啲現金要收埋，唔好畀人見到。
example.jyutping: di1 jin6 gam1 jiu3 sau1 maai4 m4 hou2 bei2 jan4 gin3 dou2

rows.note: Use this for material that has accumulated or been left on a surface, especially mineral material.

example.english: Researchers analyzed the deposit on the lakebed.
example.traditional: 研究人員分析湖底嘅沉積物。
example.jyutping: jin4 gau3 jan4 jyun4 fan1 sik1 wu4 dai2 ge3 cam4 zik1 mat6
